_meta.indication: Maintenance treatment of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) in adult patients.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, multicenter, international, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial over 24 weeks with an additional 48-week safety cohort; randomized 5:3 to ensifentrine 3 mg twice daily or placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ages 40-80 years, current or former smokers, with moderate to severe COPD.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in FEV1 AUC0-12h at Week 12.
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant increase in FEV1 AUC0-12h at Week 12 of 0.087 L vs placebo (95% CI 0.055, 0.119; p<0.0001).

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, multicenter, international, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial; single 24-week cohort with no 48-week cohort; randomized 5:3 to ensifentrine 3 mg twice daily or placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ages 40-80 years, current or former smokers, with moderate to severe COPD.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in FEV1 AUC0-12h at Week 12.
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant increase in FEV1 AUC0-12h at Week 12 of 0.094 L vs placebo (95% CI 0.067, 0.124; p<0.0001).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥1% and more common than placebo) in the pooled 24-week population (N=975 OHTUVAYRE, N=574 placebo): back pain (1.8% vs 1.0%), hypertension (1.7% vs 0.9%), urinary tract infection (1.3% vs 1.0%), and diarrhea (1.0% vs 0.7%). Discontinuations due to AEs were 7.6% vs 8.2% for placebo. Psychiatric events including suicidality were reported.
target_moa: Small molecule inhibitor of phosphodiesterase 3 (PDE3) and phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE4); inhibition increases cAMP, leading to airway smooth muscle relaxation with bronchodilation.

rems.type: No REMS is proposed at this time.

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary; there were no controversial issues.

summary.text: Standard NDA submitted under section 505(b), received June 26, 2023, and approved on the first cycle for the maintenance treatment of COPD in adults based on two adequate and well-controlled phase 3 trials (ENHANCE-1 and ENHANCE-2); no expedited designations, no REMS, and no postmarketing requirement studies.

citations.quote: Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) dated and received June 26, 2023, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Ohtuvayre (ensifentrine) inhalation suspension.
The substantial evidence of effectiveness (SEE) of ensifentrine in patients with moderate to severe COPD was established using data from two adequate and well-controlled trials.
No additional studies will be conducted as postmarketing requirements.
